Evaluate a callHow it works

Three steps, about a minute.

No setup, no template to configure. The call type and the transcript are the only two things it needs.

STEP 1

Name the call type

The call type is sent with the transcript, so the evaluation is judged against a sales call or a support call — not one generic standard.

STEP 2

Paste the transcript

Any length, any format. Speaker labels help, but raw text works. Nothing is uploaded until you press Evaluate call.

STEP 3

Read and keep the report

The report renders below the form, and the transcript is filed with it in the same record — so you can always read the feedback next to the call it came from.

What comes back.

Every report comes back in the same five sections, so two calls from two agents can actually be compared side by side.

An overall score out of 100

One number for the whole call, with a sentence explaining what drove it — enough to triage a stack of calls without opening each one.

A category table

Four to six categories scored out of 10 with a note each. The categories are chosen to fit the call type, so a support call is not graded on closing technique.

What went well, quoted

Each strength cites the actual line from the transcript, so the agent can hear the moment again instead of taking the praise on faith.

What was missed, with a fix

Every gap names where it belonged in the call and gives the better alternative — the wording the agent should have used instead.

Three actions to practise

The report closes with a numbered coaching plan a team lead can hand over as-is before the agent takes their next call.

The call kept with the review

Transcript, report, call type, and timestamp are saved as one record, each with its own page at /evaluations/[id] you can link to or revisit.
